text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Local economists have reacted with cautious optimism to the Namibian budget for 1997/98 but warned that the bloated public sector wage bill remains the government's main problem.
- Prime Minister Hage Geingob has launched an ad hoc committee to promote ethics and to help combat corruption. The committee is to investigate the adequacy of existing criminal laws and procedures.
- Namibia's Finance Minister Nangolo Mbumba announced the possible introduction of Value Added Tax (VAT) from 1998 during his budget speech on Wednesday.
- Auditor-General Fanuel Tjingaete has warned that the success of Namibia's independence depends on the eradication of corruption.
- Mbumba in his budget speech admitted lack of progress in the desired down-sizing of the civil service, saying that the problem had been carried forward into the new fiscal year.
